name: Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
preparation: Soak kombu and shiitake in the water 20 minutes, then heat gently just below a boil for 10 minutes; remove kombu, slice shiitake and return.
Add wakame and tofu, simmer 2 minutes.
Off heat, dissolve miso in a ladle of broth and stir back in — never boil miso.
Serve with spring onion.

name: Vegetable Shoyu Ramen
preparation: Simmer stock with kombu and shiitake 15 minutes; remove kombu, slice shiitake and return.
Sauté ginger and garlic in sesame oil, add to the broth with soy sauce; simmer 10 minutes.
Cook noodles separately, drain.
Blanch bok choy in the broth 1 minute.
Assemble bowls: noodles, broth, tofu, corn, bok choy, shiitake, nori, spring onion, chilli oil.

name: Kimchi Jjigae (vegetarian)
ingredients: 2 cups vegetarian kimchi (chopped, with its juice)
preparation: Sauté kimchi, onion and garlic in sesame oil 3 minutes.
Add gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce and sugar; stir 1 minute.
Add stock and mushrooms; simmer 15 minutes.
Add tofu, simmer 5 minutes; finish with spring onion. Serve with rice.

name: Sundubu Jjigae (soft tofu stew)
preparation: Sauté onion and garlic in sesame oil; add gochugaru and stir 30 seconds.
Add stock, soy sauce, sugar, mushrooms and zucchini; simmer 10 minutes.
Spoon in the silken tofu in large pieces; simmer 3 minutes without stirring hard.
Season, top with spring onion.

name: Kenchinjiru (Japanese root vegetable soup)
preparation: Sauté tofu in sesame oil until lightly browned; add carrot, daikon, taro and shiitake, stir 2 minutes.
Add stock and kombu; simmer 15 minutes until vegetables are tender; remove kombu.
Season with soy sauce and salt; serve with spring onion.

name: Vegetable Gyoza
ingredients: ½ cup finely chopped shiitake or button mushrooms
2 tbsp chopped chives or spring onion
preparation: Salt cabbage 10 minutes, squeeze dry; mix with mushrooms, tofu, chives, ginger, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Fill wrappers, wet edges, pleat and seal.
Heat oil, fry gyoza flat-side down 2 minutes until golden.
Add water, cover, steam 5 minutes until the water evaporates; serve with dipping sauce.

name: Vegetable Tempura (eggless)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (sweet potato slices, broccoli, capsicum strips, onion rings, green beans)
preparation: Whisk maida, cornflour, baking powder, salt and ice-cold water very briefly — lumps are fine.
Dip vegetables and deep-fry at 180°C in small batches 2–3 minutes until pale and crisp.
Drain on a rack; serve at once with the soy-vinegar-ginger dip.

name: Edamame with Sea Salt
preparation: Boil edamame 4–5 minutes; drain.
Toss with sesame oil, sea salt and chilli flakes; serve warm.

name: Vegetable Maki Rolls
preparation: Cook rice with water; while hot, fold in vinegar, sugar and salt; cool to room temperature.
Lay nori on a mat, spread rice thinly leaving a border, line cucumber, avocado and carrot along one edge.
Roll tightly using the mat; wet the edge to seal.
Slice with a wet knife; serve with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

name: Tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes)
preparation: Simmer stock with kombu 10 minutes; remove kombu.
Whisk in gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic.
Add rice cakes and cabbage; simmer 10 minutes stirring until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Top with spring onion and sesame seeds.

name: Korean Corn Cheese
preparation: Mix corn with mayonnaise, sugar, capsicum, salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a small skillet, add the corn mix, cook 3 minutes.
Top with mozzarella and grill or cover until melted; finish with spring onion.

name: Vietnamese Fresh Spring Rolls
preparation: Whisk peanut butter, hoisin, soy sauce, lime juice and water into a dipping sauce.
Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water 10 seconds; lay flat.
Layer lettuce, vermicelli, vegetables, herbs and tofu near one edge; fold sides in and roll tightly.
Serve with the peanut dipping sauce.

name: Agedashi Tofu
ingredients: 400 g firm tofu (pressed, cut into 8 blocks)
preparation: Simmer stock with kombu, soy sauce and sugar 5 minutes; remove kombu.
Dust tofu in cornflour; deep-fry until golden and crisp.
Place tofu in bowls, pour the hot broth around, top with ginger, daikon and spring onion.

name: Mapo Tofu (mushroom)
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed in 2 tbsp water
preparation: Fry mushrooms in oil until browned and dry.
Add doubanjiang, black bean paste, garlic and ginger; fry 1 minute until fragrant and red.
Add stock, soy sauce and sugar; simmer 2 minutes.
Slide in tofu, simmer gently 4 minutes; thicken with slurry.
Finish with Sichuan pepper, chilli oil and spring onion.

name: Teriyaki Tofu
ingredients: 1 tsp cornflour mixed in 1 tbsp water (for glaze)
preparation: Simmer soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger, garlic and water 3 minutes; thicken with the cornflour slurry into a glaze.
Dust tofu in cornflour; pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides.
Pour glaze over the tofu and turn to coat 1 minute.
Serve over rice with sesame seeds and spring onion.

name: Buddha's Delight (Lo Han Jai)
ingredients: ¼ cup dried lily buds or black fungus (soaked, optional)
1 cup vegetable stock (use shiitake soaking liquid)
1 tbsp cornflour mixed in 2 tbsp water
preparation: Sauté ginger in oil; add shiitake, carrot and bamboo, stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add cabbage, corn, snow peas, tofu puffs and fungus.
Add stock, soy sauce, mushroom sauce and sugar; simmer 8 minutes.
Thicken with slurry, finish with sesame oil.

name: Japanese Vegetable Curry (Kare)
preparation: Cook onion in oil until golden, 10 minutes; add garlic and ginger.
Add carrot, potato and pumpkin; stir 3 minutes.
Sprinkle maida and curry powder, stir 1 minute; add stock, apple, soy sauce, ketchup and sugar; simmer 25 minutes until thick.
Finish with butter, garam masala and salt. Serve over rice.

name: Vegetable Katsu (eggless)
ingredients: 200 g paneer or firm tofu (thick slabs)
preparation: Steam sweet potato and eggplant 5 minutes until just tender; pat dry.
Make a maida-water slurry; dip each piece, then coat in panko.
Deep-fry until golden; drain.
Whisk ketchup, soy sauce, sugar and mustard into a tonkatsu-style sauce; serve with shredded cabbage.

name: Nasu Dengaku (miso-glazed eggplant)
preparation: Brush eggplant with oil and roast cut-side up at 200°C for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk miso, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar and water.
Spread the glaze over the eggplant; grill 5 minutes until caramelised.
Top with sesame seeds and spring onion.

name: Braised Tofu with Shiitake
ingredients: 1 cup vegetable stock (use shiitake soaking liquid)
1 tsp cornflour mixed in 2 tbsp water
preparation: Pan-fry tofu in oil until golden on both sides; set aside.
Sauté ginger and garlic; add shiitake, both soy sauces, sugar, stock and star anise; simmer 5 minutes.
Return tofu, add bok choy; braise 8 minutes.
Thicken with slurry; finish with spring onion.

name: Mushroom and Snow Pea Stir-fry
ingredients: 300 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake, oyster mushroom, button — sliced)
1 tsp cornflour mixed in 2 tbsp water
preparation: Heat oil in a wok until smoking; sear mushrooms 3 minutes without stirring much.
Add garlic and ginger, then snow peas; stir-fry 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, mushroom sauce and sugar; thicken with slurry.
Finish with sesame oil; serve over rice.

name: Dubu Jorim (Korean braised tofu)
preparation: Pan-fry tofu in oil until golden on both sides.
Mix soy sauce, gochugaru, garlic, sugar, sesame oil and water; pour over the tofu.
Simmer 8–10 minutes, spooning sauce over, until nearly absorbed.
Top with spring onion and sesame seeds.

name: Gochujang-glazed Cauliflower
preparation: Toss florets in oil and salt; roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger and sesame oil.
Toss roasted cauliflower in the glaze; return to the oven 8 minutes until sticky.
Finish with sesame seeds and spring onion.

name: Lemongrass Tofu
preparation: Marinate tofu in lemongrass, garlic, chilli, soy sauce, sugar and lime juice 20 minutes.
Heat oil, fry onion 2 minutes; add tofu with marinade.
Stir-fry on high 6–8 minutes until browned and sticky.
Top with peanuts and coriander; serve with rice.

name: Okonomiyaki (eggless)
ingredients: 3 tbsp tonkatsu-style sauce (ketchup + soy sauce + sugar, to serve)
preparation: Whisk maida, cornflour, baking powder, salt and stock into a thick batter.
Fold in cabbage, spring onion, carrot and pickled ginger.
Cook thick pancakes in oil, covered, 5–6 minutes each side on medium.
Drizzle mayonnaise and sauce in stripes, scatter nori flakes.

name: Tofu Steak with Ginger Sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp cornflour mixed in 1 tbsp water (for sauce)
preparation: Dust tofu in cornflour; pan-fry in oil until golden and crisp on both sides.
Simmer ginger, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water 2 minutes; thicken with slurry; finish with sesame oil.
Pour sauce over the tofu; serve with broccoli and rice, topped with spring onion.

name: Bibimbap (vegetarian)
ingredients: 1 cup spinach (blanched, seasoned with ½ tsp sesame oil and a pinch of salt)
1 cup shiitake mushrooms (sliced, sautéed in 1 tsp soy sauce)
preparation: Prepare each vegetable separately — blanch spinach and sprouts, sauté carrot, zucchini and mushrooms, pan-fry tofu.
Whisk gochujang, sesame oil, vinegar and sugar into the sauce.
Mound rice in bowls, arrange vegetables and tofu in sections on top.
Add sauce and sesame seeds; mix everything together to eat.

name: Kimbap (vegetable)
ingredients: 200 g firm tofu (long strips, pan-fried with 1 tbsp soy sauce)
preparation: Season warm rice with sesame oil and salt; cool slightly.
Spread rice over nori leaving a border; lay spinach, carrot, radish, cucumber and tofu along one edge.
Roll tightly, brush the outside with a little sesame oil.
Slice into rounds; sprinkle sesame seeds.

name: Japchae (glass noodles)
preparation: Boil noodles 6–7 minutes until chewy; drain, rinse, toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp sesame oil.
Sauté each vegetable separately in oil with a pinch of salt; wilt spinach last.
Combine noodles, vegetables, garlic, remaining soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil in a large bowl; toss well.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sesame seeds.

name: Yaki Udon
preparation: Cook udon per packet, drain.
Stir-fry onion, cabbage, carrot and mushrooms in oil 3 minutes on high.
Add udon, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar; toss 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil, spring onion, pickled ginger and nori.

name: Vegetable Yakisoba
preparation: Boil noodles until just done; drain.
Whisk soy sauce, ketchup, sugar and vinegar into the sauce.
Stir-fry onion, cabbage, carrot and capsicum 3 minutes on high.
Add noodles and sauce; toss 2 minutes; top with spring onion and pickled ginger.

name: Kimchi Fried Rice (vegetarian)
preparation: Sauté onion and garlic in oil; add kimchi and cook 3 minutes.
Add gochujang, soy sauce and kimchi juice; stir.
Add rice and toss on high 3 minutes; fold in tofu.
Finish with sesame oil, spring onion, sesame seeds and nori.

name: Mushroom Donburi
ingredients: 1 tsp cornflour mixed in 1 tbsp water
preparation: Sauté onion in oil until soft; add mushrooms and brown 4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger and stock; simmer 3 minutes; thicken with slurry.
Spoon over bowls of rice; top with spring onion and nori.

name: Vegetable Lo Mein
ingredients: 400 g lo mein or hakka noodles (egg-free)
2 cups mixed vegetables (capsicum, carrot, snow peas, mushroom, bok choy)
preparation: Boil noodles until just done; drain and toss with sesame oil.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger and vegetables 3 minutes on high.
Add noodles, both soy sauces, mushroom sauce and sugar; toss 2 minutes.
Finish with spring onion.

name: Dan Dan Noodles (vegetarian)
preparation: Fry mushrooms in oil until browned; add garlic, ginger and 1 tbsp soy sauce; set aside.
Whisk sesame paste, chilli oil, remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and stock into the sauce; divide among bowls.
Boil noodles, drain, add to bowls.
Top with mushrooms, bok choy, peanuts and spring onion; mix to eat.

name: Pho Chay (Vietnamese vegetable pho)
ingredients: ½ cup fresh basil and coriander
preparation: Simmer stock with charred onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves and coriander seeds 30 minutes; strain; season with soy sauce, sugar and salt.
Soak or boil rice noodles per packet; drain.
Simmer mushrooms in the broth 3 minutes.
Assemble bowls with noodles, tofu, broth; top with sprouts, herbs, lime and chilli.

name: Zaru Soba with Dipping Sauce
preparation: Simmer stock with kombu, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar 5 minutes; remove kombu; chill the dipping sauce.
Boil soba per packet; rinse under cold water and drain well.
Serve noodles on a plate topped with nori and sesame; dip into the sauce with spring onion and wasabi.

name: Vietnamese Tofu Bún (noodle bowl)
ingredients: ½ cup fresh mint and coriander
preparation: Whisk the dressing ingredients until sugar dissolves.
Toss tofu in soy sauce and lemongrass; pan-fry in oil until crisp.
Cook vermicelli per packet; rinse and drain.
Layer lettuce, noodles, vegetables, tofu and herbs in bowls; pour over dressing, top with peanuts.

name: Steamed Bao Buns
preparation: Mix maida, yeast, sugar, baking powder, salt, milk and oil; knead 8 minutes; rest 1 hour.
Divide into 10, roll into ovals, brush with oil, fold in half over a chopstick; rest 20 minutes on paper squares.
Steam 10–12 minutes; fill with teriyaki tofu or braised mushrooms.

name: Scallion Pancakes
preparation: Mix maida, salt and hot water into a dough; knead smooth, rest 30 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with sesame oil, scatter spring onion, roll into a log, coil, and roll flat again.
Pan-fry in oil 3 minutes each side until golden and flaky.

name: Sigeumchi Namul (Korean seasoned spinach)
preparation: Blanch spinach 30 seconds; plunge in cold water, squeeze dry, chop.
Toss with garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, sesame seeds, spring onion and salt.

name: Sesame Broccoli
preparation: Blanch broccoli 2 minutes; drain.
Heat oil, cook garlic until pale gold; add broccoli, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar; toss 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil, sesame seeds and chilli flakes.

name: Vegetarian Kimchi
ingredients: 1 large napa cabbage (cut into 5 cm pieces)
2 tbsp rice flour mixed in ½ cup water (cooked into a paste, cooled)
preparation: Dissolve salt in water; soak cabbage 1½ hours, turning; rinse well and drain.
Mix gochugaru, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sugar and the rice-flour paste into a thick red paste.
Combine cabbage, daikon, carrot and spring onion with the paste, working it into every leaf.
Pack tightly into a jar, leaving 2 cm headspace; ferment at room temperature 1–3 days, then refrigerate. No fish sauce or shrimp — fully vegetarian.

name: Sunomono (Japanese cucumber salad)
preparation: Salt cucumber 10 minutes; squeeze out water.
Whisk vinegar, sugar and soy sauce; toss with cucumber and wakame.
Chill; serve with sesame seeds.

name: Oi Muchim (Korean spicy cucumber salad)
preparation: Toss cucumber with salt 5 minutes; drain.
Mix with gochugaru, garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, sesame seeds and spring onion.
Serve immediately or chilled.

name: Citrus Soy Dipping Sauce (ponzu-style)
ingredients: ¼ cup lemon or lime juice
preparation: Warm soy sauce, water, sugar and kombu gently 3 minutes; remove kombu.
Cool; stir in citrus juice and vinegar.
Keeps refrigerated 2 weeks; use for gyoza, tempura and tofu.

name: Mango Pudding (agar-set)
preparation: Whisk agar-agar into the water; boil 2 minutes stirring.
Stir in sugar, milk and cream; simmer 1 minute; off heat, blend in mango pulp.
Pour into cups, chill 3 hours until set; top with diced mango.

name: Sesame Balls (Jian Dui)
preparation: Dissolve sugar in hot water; mix into the rice flour to a soft dough.
Divide into 12, flatten, wrap around a ball of red bean paste, seal and roll smooth.
Roll in sesame seeds, pressing to stick.
Deep-fry on medium-low, pressing gently as they puff, until golden and crisp.

name: Daifuku Mochi
ingredients: ¾ cup sweet red bean paste
preparation: Whisk rice flour, sugar and water; microwave or steam, stirring every minute, until thick and translucent (about 4 minutes).
Turn onto a cornflour-dusted board; divide into 8 while warm.
Flatten each piece, wrap around a ball of red bean paste, pinch to seal.
Dust off excess cornflour; eat the same day.

name: Matcha Latte
preparation: Whisk matcha with hot water until frothy and lump-free.
Heat milk with sugar until steaming; froth if you can.
Pour milk over the matcha; serve hot or over ice.
